judged_text: createEvent builds the Graph events URL from mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId — the first destination calendar — while EventManager now invokes createEvent once per host credential, so every host's token targets the first host's calendar id. Collective bookings with multiple Office 365 hosts (the exact case this PR adds) POST to /me/calendars/{firstHostCalendarId}/events with each secondary host's token; Graph returns 404 for a calendar outside that host's mailbox and the event is never created on the secondary host's calendar, leaving their slot booked in Cal.com but empty on their calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now derives `eventsUrl` from `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and uses only that first calendar’s `externalId` (`/me/calendars/{mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId}/events`). Meanwhile `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` was changed to iterate over `event.destinationCalendar` and call `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` per destination/host credential, but `CalendarManager.createEvent` only passes `credential.id` into `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` and Office365’s implementation ignores the per-destination externalId entirely. With collective events, `handleNewBooking` constructs `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array starting with organizer’s calendar then pushes other hosts’ destination calendars, so secondary hosts will still POST to the organizer’s calendar id using their own token, which can 404 and skip creating the secondary host’s event.
